audit_scope: Existing small manifests/summaries and bounded game header/tail reads; no new searches, ratings fits, bulk-game parsing, tests, builds, or source edits.
recommendation: Existing H bounded quiet/capture history has actual completed-game evidence. Relative-history normalization and cost-aware move ordering remain untested follow-ups in this audited evidence; do not conflate them with H, continuation history, q-history, or clock growth policy.

bounded_history_H.policy: Bounded positive/negative quiet history and capture history, ordering only, per-search through iterative deepening; not an attempts-normalized relative history and not cost-aware ordering.
bounded_history_H.rating_method: Bradley-Terry; equal game weights; draws=half; mean=1500
bounded_history_H.selection: Twelve original game records in six complete color-swapped pairs against the four highest-rated eligible opponents with complete pairs available. Retain variety (at most two pairs per opponent); assign remaining pairs to higher-rated opponents and break ties in favor of older slots. Outcomes are not a selection criterion.
caveats: Only one archived two-game pair is counted here; not all H games in the rating fit.
The reported fit has no uncertainty interval or per-H sample count in this small manifest.
Higher-rated-opponent selection is not random. Rating points and the pair outcomes do not estimate a causal improvement or validate another history formulation.
These games precede the permanent-progress correction and use the preserved legacy live search; applicability to current main is limited.

history_combinations.selection: Six complete same-start color-swapped pairs; at least four opponents; at most two pairs per opponent. Maximize summed current opponent ratings subject to these constraints, then select the oldest completed pairs for each opponent by latest game-file modification time. Outcomes are not a selection criterion.

policy_mapping.HLF_CH: HLF + one-previous-move continuation history; not relative normalization or cost-aware ordering

caveats: All HLF/HLFS comparisons combine policies; no isolated H effect.
The HLF_CH 2-0 result against HLF is one selected pair, not a continuation-history verdict.
Archived sample and opponent rating fit do not supply error bars or current-running status.

generation3_capped_screen.comparator: ContextRetry on the same HLF or HLFS parent in the same candidate binary
generation3_capped_screen.method: One capped search per case/arm. Highest shared completed depth per comparison, cumulative nodes through depth, comparator ContextRetry on same parent. Ratios describe this convenience corpus only; depths vary by comparison; no playing-strength or isolated-time claim. GA has no Fischer soft budget here and tests common context only. PR screen predates stricter exact-bound classification and requires final rerun.
caveats: Single capped request per case/arm; no repeated timing uncertainty.
Ratios are cumulative nodes at highest shared completed depth, not NPS, elapsed-time speedup, or playing strength.
QH reuses existing capture history in q ordering; it does not test relative-history normalization or cost-aware ordering.
GA has no Fischer soft budget in these requests, so its clock mechanism is inactive.
Convenience corpus with correlated turns and game-length weighting.
Incomplete-iteration share measures summed recorded iteration time, not recoverable speed or whole-game time.
This motivates clock/partial-iteration work; it is not a cost-aware move-ordering experiment.
